etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English if, yif, yef, from Old English ġif (“if”), from Proto-West Germanic *jabu, *jabē, from Proto-Germanic *jabai (“when, if”). Cognate with Scots gif (“if, whether”), Saterland Frisian af, of (“if, whether”), West Frisian oft (“whether”), Dutch of (“or, whether, but”), Middle Low German ef, if, af, of ("if; whether"; > German Low German of), German ob (“if, whether”), Icelandic ef (“if”).

definitions.definition: (computing) A keyword that invokes conditional processing: in the event that a given condition is true, execute the given statement(s) (otherwise execute other statements).
Supposing that, assuming that, in the circumstances that; used to introduce a condition that may be (or prove to be) either true or false.
(usually hyperbolic) Even if; even in the circumstances that.

quote.citation: 1838, Boz [pseudonym; Charles Dickens], Oliver Twist; or, The Parish Boy’s Progress. […], volume (please specify |volume=I, II, or III), London: Richard Bentley, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: “Wait a minute!” said the girl: “I wouldn’t hurry by, if it was you that was coming out to be hung, the next time eight o’clock struck, Bill. I’d walk round and round the place till I dropped, if the snow was on the ground, and I hadn’t a shawl to cover me.”

quote.citation: 2004, David Lee Murphy and Kim Tribble (writers), Montgomery Gentry (singers), “If It’s The Last Thing I Do” (song), in You Do Your Thing (album):
quote.text: If it’s the last thing I do / If it takes me from Tubilo to Timbuktu / If it’s the last thing I do / I’m gonna dodge every road block, speed trap, county cop / To get my hands on you / If it’s the last thing I do.

definitions.definition: Supposing that; used with past or past perfect subjunctive to indicate a counterfactual or hypothetical condition.
Considering the fact that; given that; introducing a condition that is known to be true.

quote.citation: 1596, Edmund Spenser, “Book I”, in The Faerie Queene. […], part I (books I–III), London:  […]  [Richard Field] for William Ponsonbie, →OCLC, stanza ii, page 66:
quote.text: O what of Gods then boots it to be borne, / If old Aveugles ſonnes ſo euill heare?

definitions.definition: Although; used to introduce a concession.

quote.citation: 1981 April 11, Mitzel, “Kopacz Acquitted In Barbre Killing”, in Gay Community News, page 1:
quote.text: Both Spear & Davis were indicted in the witchhunt surrounding the sensational (if nonexistent) "Revere sex ring."

definitions.definition: (sometimes proscribed) Whether; used to introduce a noun clause, an indirect question, that functions as the direct object of certain verbs.

quote.citation: 1715–1717, Matthew Prior, Alma; or, The Progress of the Mind, Canto III:
quote.text: Quoth Matthew, “ […]  / She doubts if two and two make four, /  […] ”

quote.citation: 1976, Michael Harrison, Beyond Baker Street: A Sherlockian Anthology, page 117:
quote.text: It is doubtful if the Victorian Londoner needed any warning, for the artful mobsmen, toolers, whizzers and dippers, together with their stickman accomplices, were everywhere in the crowds, in the underground, on railway trains  […]

definitions.definition: (informal) An uncertainty, possibility, condition, doubt etc.

quote.citation: 1709, Susannah Centlivre, The Busy Body, Act III, in John Bell (ed.), British Theater, J. Bell (1791), page 59,
quote.text: Sir Fran. Nay, but Chargy, if——— ¶ Miran. Nay, Gardy, no Ifs.——Have I refus'd three northern lords, two British peers, and half a score knights, to have put in your Ifs?

quote.citation: 1791 January, “Richardſon’s Chemical Principles of the Metallic Arts”, in The Monthly Review, R. Griffiths, page 176:
quote.text: Well might Bergman add, (in his Sciographia,),  “if the compariſon that has been made, &c. be juſt.” The preſent writer makes no ifs  about the matter, and has ſuperadded a little inaccuracy of his own, […]

quote.citation: 2013 April 9, Andrei Lankov, “Stay Cool. Call North Korea’s Bluff.”, in New York Times‎[1]:
quote.text: Even if they managed to strike Japan, the United States or South Korea with nuclear weapons — a big if, given that they do not have a reliable delivery system — they could not save themselves from ultimate defeat.
